questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Germany?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Germany article.

questions.proof: During this time, the capital city of Berlin was divided into a west and an east part.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Germany?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Germany on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Germany article.

questions.proof: The highest point is the Zugspitze on the Austrian border, at 2,962 metres (9,718 ft).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the east of Germany are the countries of _____ and the Czech Republic.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “countries”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Germany article.

questions.proof: To the east of Germany are the countries of Poland and the Czech Republic.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “For example, in the southern regions, such as Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, they share their type of food with _____ and Austria.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “food”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Food” part of the Germany article.

questions.proof: For example, in the southern regions, such as Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, they share their type of food with Switzerland and Austria.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the north of Germany are the North Sea and the Baltic Sea, and the kingdom of _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “kingdom”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Germany article.

questions.proof: To the north of Germany are the North Sea and the Baltic Sea, and the kingdom of Denmark.
